title: Little Drops of Water
source_note: NCERT structural and thematic alignment only. All teaching passages, checks, feedback, and assessment situations are original Zidd content.

levels.title: See how little parts grow
levels.focus: identify how many small parts can make something large
levels.teaching_goal: Join examples of drops, grains, minutes, and deeds into the chapter's cumulative main idea.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea covers every sentence. One drop is small, but repeated drops change the amount.
guided_check.passage: Meera adds one spoon of water to a jar each morning. By the end of the week, the jar holds enough water for three plants.
guided_check.prompt: Which idea fits the whole passage?
options: Small amounts can build into a useful amount.
Plants need a new jar each day.
One spoon fills every jar at once.
accepted_answers: Small amounts can build into a useful amount.
small amounts build into a useful amount

bridge.teaching_block: Look for repeated small parts and the larger result. Do not focus only on who brings the first part.
bridge.passage: Each child brings a handful of soil. Together, the handfuls fill the new planter.

masterclass.teaching_block: The same pattern works with time. Many short practice periods can create progress.
masterclass.passage: Asha reads for five minutes every evening. After a month, she can finish a short book by herself.
masterclass.prompt: What main idea does this example show?
accepted_answers: small efforts can lead to progress
short practice can make a big difference

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain both the small repeated action and the larger result. Wording may differ, but both parts are needed.
independent_check.passage: Every day, a family saves one clean bottle for recycling. At month's end, they take a full sack to the collection centre.
independent_check.prompt: How do the family's small actions add up?

concept_slots.description: Mention saving one bottle each day.
Mention the full sack or recycling collection.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the cumulative idea to money for a class goal. Include the repeated saving and the final purchase.
transfer_check.passage: A club places two coins in a box after every meeting. Months later, there is enough money to buy a magnifying glass.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain how the club reaches its goal.

concept_slots.description: Mention adding two coins repeatedly.
Mention buying the magnifying glass.

levels.title: Connect a small action to its effect
levels.focus: infer how one repeated choice helps or harms over time
levels.teaching_goal: Use cause-and-effect clues to explain why small choices matter when repeated.

guided_check.teaching_block: Find the repeated cause and the later effect. A single day is not the whole explanation.
guided_check.passage: Ira loosens the soil around a sapling for two minutes each day. New roots spread more easily, and the plant becomes stronger.
guided_check.prompt: Why does the sapling become stronger?
options: Two minutes is a long time.
accepted_answers: ira loosens the soil every day
because the soil is loosened each day

bridge.teaching_block: Small harmful actions also add up. Choose the cause that happens repeatedly.
bridge.passage: Someone leaves one plastic straw near the pond each afternoon. Soon many straws block the water's edge.
bridge.prompt: What causes the edge to become blocked?
options: Straws are left there again and again.
accepted_answers: Straws are left there again and again.
one straw is left each afternoon

masterclass.teaching_block: Kindness can have a chain effect. Identify the first small act that changes what happens next.
masterclass.passage: Mukul moves aside so an elderly passenger can sit. Another child notices and makes room for a parent with a baby.
masterclass.prompt: What starts the chain of helpful actions?
accepted_answers: Mukul lets the elderly passenger sit

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the cause and effect without copying the passage. Include the repeated habit and the result.
independent_check.passage: Lina writes one new spelling on a card every day and reviews the cards on Sunday. After several weeks, she spells many more words correctly.

concept_slots.description: Mention the repeated card practice.
Mention improved spelling.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply cause and effect to sleep habits. Name the small repeated choice and the daytime result.
transfer_check.passage: For a week, Jai goes to bed ten minutes earlier. He begins waking on time and feels alert in class.
transfer_check.prompt: How does Jai's small change help him?

concept_slots.description: Mention going to bed earlier repeatedly.
Mention waking on time or feeling alert.

levels.title: Understand words about amount and care
levels.focus: use context for drop, grain, deed, mighty, and shared
levels.teaching_goal: Infer small-amount and kindness words from concrete clues, including an explicit target whenever shared is assessed.

guided_check.teaching_block: A drop is a very small amount of liquid. The clue is that it hangs at the tip before falling.
guided_check.passage: One clear drop hangs from the tap and falls into the cup.

bridge.teaching_block: A grain is one tiny piece of a dry food or material. The many rice pieces provide the clue.
bridge.passage: One grain of rice slips from the spoon; hundreds remain in the bowl.

masterclass.teaching_block: A deed is something a person does. A kind deed is a helpful action, not merely a kind thought.
masterclass.passage: Holding the gate for a neighbour is a small deed that makes carrying bags easier.

independent_check.teaching_block: Shared must have a clear target. Here the art tools are shared because every table may use the same box.
independent_check.passage: The class has one shared box of crayons. Children from every table take turns using it and return it for the next group.
independent_check.prompt: What does shared tell us about the crayon box?
accepted_answers: it is for all the children

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the word mighty to a transport scene. The result shows great strength, not large size alone.
transfer_check.passage: The small engine pulls six heavy coaches up the hill. It is mighty despite its size.

levels.title: Choose words for small helpful acts
levels.focus: use deed, kindness, gather, and together in meaningful sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Select a chapter word by the action and result in the sentence, not by rhyme or familiarity.

guided_check.teaching_block: A deed is an action. When the action helps someone, kind describes the deed.
guided_check.passage: Carrying a neighbour's parcel is a helpful ____.
guided_check.prompt: Which word names this helpful action?

bridge.teaching_block: Gather means bring separate things together. It fits before the objects form one collection.
bridge.passage: The children ____ fallen seeds into one bowl.

masterclass.teaching_block: Together shows people joining their efforts. It is not the same as each person working alone in a different place.
masterclass.passage: The two teams work ____ to carry the long mat.
masterclass.prompt: Which action finishes the juice clean-up?

independent_check.teaching_block: Kindness names caring behaviour. The clue is the comfort given to another person.
independent_check.passage: A warm note to a lonely friend shows ____.
independent_check.prompt: Which words tell how to handle the empty packet?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use two chapter words in a new emergency-drive context. Show many people combining small contributions.
transfer_check.passage: Families each bring one soap bar for a relief box. Soon the box is full.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one sentence about the collection using two suitable chapter words.

concept_slots.description: Use a word for combined effort.
Refer to the small contributions building up.

levels.title: Link little actions and results
levels.focus: use because for causes and but for surprising contrasts
levels.teaching_goal: Join chapter ideas with because or but according to the relationship between them.

guided_check.teaching_block: Because introduces the cause. The second part explains why the pot fills.
guided_check.passage: The pot fills slowly ____ one cup is added every day.
guided_check.prompt: Which connector belongs in the blank?

bridge.teaching_block: But shows a contrast: small size is followed by a large effect.
bridge.passage: The seed is tiny, ____ it can grow into a tall plant.

masterclass.teaching_block: Ask whether the second part is a reason. Here it explains why the shelf has many books.
masterclass.passage: The reading shelf grows ____ each family adds one storybook.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use but when the result is stronger than the small beginning might suggest.
independent_check.passage: The note was short, ____ it cheered Maya all afternoon.
independent_check.prompt: Which connector shows the short note's surprising effect?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer both links to a health routine. Use because for the reason and but for the small-to-large contrast.
transfer_check.passage: Rohan stretches for a few minutes every morning. After many days, bending feels easier.
transfer_check.prompt: Write two connected sentences, one with because and one with but.

concept_slots.description: Use because to link practice and improvement.
Use but to contrast a few minutes with the larger effect.
Refer to stretching or easier bending.

levels.title: Summarize the little-things message
levels.focus: state how small acts add up and give a relevant example
levels.teaching_goal: Write a short original summary with the cumulative idea and one supported example.

guided_check.teaching_block: A summary gives the big idea, not every detail. Choose the sentence that joins repeated small parts and a larger result.
guided_check.passage: One bead is added to a string each day. At the end of the month, the class has a long decoration.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary?
options: Small daily additions can make something large.
accepted_answers: Small daily additions can make something large.
small daily additions can make something large

bridge.teaching_block: A reason answer explains why a little act matters. Select the effect supported by the passage.
bridge.passage: Anu greets the new child each morning. Soon the child enters class with a smile.
options: They help the new child feel welcome.
accepted_answers: They help the new child feel welcome.
they help the new child feel welcome
they make the child feel welcome

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass check: include both the small action and its larger effect in a concise sentence.
masterclass.passage: Each neighbour plants one marigold along the lane. In a few weeks, flowers line the whole path.
accepted_answers: Small actions can make a big difference.
small actions can make a big difference
Many small acts create a big result.

independent_check.teaching_block: Summarize in your own words. State the little-things idea and use the given reading example as support.
independent_check.passage: Navi reads one page aloud to his brother each night. By summer, they have enjoyed an entire storybook together.
independent_check.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the lesson in this scene.

concept_slots.description: State that small repeated efforts add up.
Mention pages building into a whole book.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the chapter message to a new digital habit. Include the repeated action and its useful result.
transfer_check.passage: Sana learns one keyboard shortcut each Friday. After a term, she can finish her computer work more quickly.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain how this new context shows the chapter's message.

concept_slots.description: Mention learning one shortcut regularly.
Mention faster computer work.

items.passage: One tile is painted each afternoon. After two weeks, the wall has a bright border.
items.prompt: Which statement captures what the daily painting achieves?
options: Small repeated work can create a larger result.
A wall must be painted in one day.
accepted_answers: Small repeated work can create a larger result.
small repeated work creates a larger result

items.passage: Each student learns one line of a song. Together, the class can perform the whole song.
items.prompt: What do the separate lines allow the class to do?
options: The class performs the whole song.
accepted_answers: The class performs the whole song.

items.passage: A gardener adds a little compost every Saturday. Months later, the soil is dark and rich.
items.prompt: Explain how the small actions add up.

concept_slots.description: Mention adding a little compost regularly.
Mention the improved soil.

items.passage: The class writes one thank-you card each week. By term end, every helper has received one.
items.prompt: State the main idea in your own words.

concept_slots.description: State that repeated small acts reach a larger goal.
Mention all helpers receiving thanks.

items.passage: Naman practises tying one knot every evening. Soon he can secure the tent rope by himself.
items.prompt: Why can Naman secure the rope?

items.passage: A dripping tap loses a little water each minute. By morning, the bucket below is full.
items.prompt: What causes the bucket to fill?

items.passage: Every visitor steps off the path to take a shortcut. After many visits, the young grass is flattened.
items.prompt: Explain why the grass becomes flat.

concept_slots.description: Mention repeated footsteps or shortcuts.
Mention the grass being flattened or damaged.

items.passage: Priya smiles at one nervous speaker. The speaker relaxes and finishes the poem aloud.
items.prompt: How does Priya's small act help?

concept_slots.description: Mention Priya's encouraging smile.
Mention the speaker relaxing or finishing.

items.passage: One grain of sand sticks to the wet shell; many more cover the beach.
items.prompt: What does grain mean?

items.passage: The small tugboat is mighty enough to pull a huge ship.
items.prompt: Which meaning fits mighty?

items.passage: Offering your seat to someone who needs it is a caring deed.
items.prompt: In this example, what kind of thing is a deed?

items.passage: The garden hose is shared: every family on the lane may borrow it and returns it after use.
items.prompt: What does shared mean for the hose?
accepted_answers: it is for everyone on the lane

items.passage: Helping a younger child carry books is a kind ____.
items.prompt: Choose the chapter word.

items.passage: The scouts ____ dry leaves into a compost sack.
items.prompt: Which action completes the sentence?

items.passage: The players lift the net ____.
items.prompt: Write the word that means as one group.

items.passage: Listening patiently to a worried friend shows ____.
items.prompt: Complete the sentence with a caring word.

items.passage: The tank rises slowly ____ rainwater enters through a pipe.
items.prompt: Choose the reason connector.

items.passage: The ladybird is tiny, ____ it eats many plant pests.
items.prompt: Which connector shows contrast?

items.passage: The song grows louder ____ another voice joins each verse.
items.prompt: Write the connector that introduces the cause.

items.passage: The patch is small, ____ it keeps the water bag from leaking.
items.prompt: Which word links the small patch to its strong effect?

items.passage: Every evening, Ben adds one puzzle piece. At last, the complete picture covers the board.
items.prompt: Choose the best summary.
options: Small daily steps can complete a large task.
The board is made of wood.
One piece is the whole picture.
accepted_answers: Small daily steps can complete a large task.
small daily steps complete a large task

items.passage: Leela waves to the crossing guard each day. The guard feels noticed and smiles back.
items.prompt: Why does Leela's small act matter?
options: It helps the guard feel appreciated.
accepted_answers: It helps the guard feel appreciated.
it makes the guard feel appreciated

items.passage: A team folds one paper flower at every club meeting. Soon they have enough to decorate the hall.
items.prompt: Summarize the lesson in this scene.

concept_slots.description: State that small repeated work adds up.
Mention enough flowers to decorate the hall.

items.passage: Kiran puts one useful fact on a study card each day. Before the quiz, he has a full set to review.
items.prompt: Explain how this example shows the chapter's message.

concept_slots.description: Mention adding one fact daily.
Mention the full review set.
